$comment: The published subpath contract, as data (TASK-R1-O2). validate:exports proves every DECLARED target resolves; it never noticed a subpath being DELETED, because a package with fewer exports still has zero broken ones. This file closes that: the set of subpaths a published package offers is a promise, and under packages/contracts/VERSIONING.md (0.x) removing one is a breaking change — a `minor` bump and a changeset, never a silent edit. Adding one is equally deliberate: a new subpath must be listed here, which is where its reason for existing gets written down. Only the six packages in release-policy.json `published` are governed; withheld and private packages are free to move.
$howToChange: Removing a subpath: delete it here, write the changeset (`minor` under 0.x), and say in the changeset which import path stops working. Adding one: append it with a reason, and add a `patch` changeset. Never edit this file to make a red gate green without doing one of those two things.

@dzup-ui/contracts.$reason: Types-first, one entry. A subpath here would fragment the contract the two tiers share.

@dzup-ui/core.$reason: The root barrel plus the seams a host reaches without pulling the component barrel, plus the eleven family subpaths a bundler-less consumer imports from directly.

notes../i18n: TASK-R5-O4 / N5-04 D4. The localisation surface — `useDzMessageFormat` and the message-group types. Three import paths failed with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED before it existed, which blocked every locale pack and made ADR-20's i18n promises unverifiable. It is snapshotted here because the defect it fixes is invisible from inside the repository: source imports keep working after the exports entry is gone.
notes../i18n/locales/en.json: The English catalog ships as JSON data, not as a named export — what a translator and a translation-management tool edit, and what keeps a second language out of every bundle. A locale pack's import path is part of the contract exactly as the composable's is.
notes../styles: ADR-15 / the five-layer contract: `import '@dzup-ui/core/styles'` is the documented way to load the built CSS. It was declared for months while the build emitted no CSS at all (the defect that produced export-map.ts).

@dzup-ui/mcp.$reason: A public package governed through mcp-tool-surface.json. `./registry` is the client an embedder reuses without starting the server.

@dzup-ui/nuxt.$reason: A Nuxt module: one entry, resolved by `modules: ['@dzup-ui/nuxt']`.

@dzup-ui/testing.$reason: The consumer-facing test kit. `./vitest` is a setup module imported for its effect (see published-imports-policy.json); `./security-corpus` is the shared attack corpus TASK-R3-O4 formalises across the two repositories.

@dzup-ui/tokens.$reason: The token ABI: the JS scales, the two stylesheets, the DTCG document (ADR-19's interchange format) and the Tailwind theme.

notes../dtcg: ADR-19's interchange promise. A design tool reads this path; nothing inside the repository does, so only a snapshot notices it disappearing.
